title: Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act 1960 — Member Rights & Governance
description: Key provisions governing registration, annual general meetings, committee elections, and audit requirements under Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act.
source_name: Department of Co-operation, Marketing & Textiles, Govt of Maharashtra
content:
The Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960 governs the registration, regulation, management, and audit of all cooperative societies in the state of Maharashtra.

Key Provisions:
1. Society Registration: Minimum number of eligible members required to register a cooperative society varies by category (e.g., housing, agricultural credit, sugar cooperatives).
2. Member Rights: Every member has the right to vote in general body meetings (one member, one vote principle), inspect society registers, receive audited financial statements, and contest committee elections if compliant with contribution and attendance norms.
3. Annual General Meeting (AGM): The Managing Committee must convene an AGM within the statutory period (typically before September 30 each year) to present annual accounts, audit reports, surplus distribution plans, and appoint auditors.
4. Audit Mandate: Accounts of every cooperative society must be audited annually by a certified auditor approved by the Registrar of Cooperative Societies.
5. Dispute Resolution & Grievance: Disputes relating to society constitution, elections, management, or business must be referred to the Cooperative Court or District Registrar as specified under Section 91 of the Act.
